renderings.value: Used to express 'even though one wants to do something, one can't for some reason'.
The ～ようにも grammar point indicates that a person wants or tries to do something (volitional form), but for some reason cannot. Often, there's a second clause explaining what prevents the action.
Verb-volitional form + にも + (reason/potential negative, etc.)

ようにも～ない: can't even if you want to (行こうにも行けない). The attachment differs: Verb-volitional + にも is 'even if I try to V, I can't' (走ろうにも走れない), Verb-dictionary + にも is 'even to V, the means are lacking' (受けるにもお金が足りない).
I'd like to run a bit faster, but I can’t because my leg hurts.
I want to talk to him, but he's ignoring me.
I want to study more, but I have no time.
I would like to apologize to her, but she's already angry.
Even if it rains tomorrow, I have too much luggage to bring an umbrella.
I failed the exam, but I don’t have the money to take it again even if I wanted to.
Even if I want to see him, it's a difficult situation to meet him.
I'd need a taxi to get from this airport to her house, even if I wanted to go.
